Today's big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

Carvana sells used cars online, and it lends many of its buyers the money to pay for them. Last quarter it sold 217,385 cars, 39% more than a year earlier. Its sales over the last 12 months reached $27.5 billion, up 50%.

Analysts expect sales to grow another 27% next year. That would be faster than every Consumer Discretionary company worth more than $50 billion except MercadoLibre. Yet 14 of those 21 companies cost more than Carvana per dollar of sales, from Amazon to McDonald's. Carvana's market value is 2.9 times its sales. Three things explain that low price: the yardstick, the stock's fall in 2022, and car loans.

Is Carvana Really Cheap?

Only per dollar of sales. Selling a car brings in a lot of money but leaves a thin profit. Over the last 12 months, Carvana kept 19 cents per dollar of sales after the cost of the cars. It kept 8.7 cents of operating profit, what is left after all running costs. McDonald's kept 46.1 cents of operating profit per dollar.

On operating profit, Carvana's market value is 32.7 times, more than investors pay for Home Depot or McDonald's. Carvana has two classes of shares, and its market value here counts both.

Of the 21 peers, 18 cost less than Carvana per dollar of operating profit. Only Tesla, DoorDash and Airbnb cost more. Priced on net profit, Carvana's 33 times is also above most of them. CarMax costs 0.3 times sales but made an operating loss. So Carvana's low price per dollar of sales comes from the yardstick. It is not a bargain. On profit, Carvana is not cheap. Buyers who want a lower price may have to wait. Meanwhile, the Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3x the S&P 500's. It holds 50 stocks with at least 10 straight years of dividends. See if it fits.

Why Won't Investors Pay Up For The Growth?

Because they watched the stock fall 99%. In 2022, sales growth stalled. Gross margin, the share of sales left after the cost of the cars, fell to 9.2% from 15.1%. Carvana lost $1.5 billion on its operations, and its debt climbed to $8.8 billion.

title: Booking Holdings vs. MercadoLibre: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:
Booking Holdings vs. MercadoLibre: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Brendan Coffey, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 8:10 AM MST 7 min read
BKNG
MELI
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors often choose between proven global leaders and high-growth regional powerhouses. Deciding between Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:BKNG) and MercadoLibre Inc. (NASDAQ:MELI) requires weighing stable profitability against an expanding digital ecosystem in Latin America.

Booking serves the global travel market through its massive network of accommodations and flight options. MercadoLibre dominates Latin American e-commerce and digital payments, functioning as both a retailer and a bank. While both companies operate in the consumer discretionary space, they offer very different risk-reward profiles for long-term investors looking toward 2027.

The case for Booking Holdings

Booking operates a massive network of consumer-facing brands, including Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, and OpenTable. The company focuses on its "connected trip" strategy, which aims to integrate accommodations, flights, and rental cars into a single, seamless itinerary for travelers. By managing nearly 4.7 million accommodation properties, it relies on a broad network of travel service providers that typically operate on non-exclusive terms.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $28.1 billion, representing roughly 8% growth compared to the prior year. The company reported net income of approximately $7.2 billion, reflecting a net margin of about 25.5%. This performance demonstrates the company's ability to generate significant profit while expanding its presence in the international travel market.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company carries a negative debt-to-equity ratio of roughly -3.5x, indicating that its total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. The debt-to-equity ratio, which compares total debt to the equity held by shareholders, measures how a business balances its obligations against its assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow, which is cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures, was about $9.1 billion.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre operates the leading commerce and fintech ecosystem in Latin America, driven by the Mercado Libre marketplace and its Mercado Pago payment platform. As a leader among consumer discretionary stocks in its region, it relies on a vast network of third-party sellers and logistics partners. Its integrated strategy combines retail, lending, and asset management to serve over 136 million unique buyers.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $38.5 billion, marking about 47% growth over the previous period. The company reported net income of approximately $1.9 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 4.9%. This rapid top-line expansion highlights the scaling nature of its integrated digital services across major markets like Brazil and Mexico.

MercadoLibre: Maintaining a Steady Upward Revenue Expansion

MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) primarily earns its revenue by operating a prominent digital commerce marketplace alongside a complementary financial technology platform that facilitates secure digital transactions and credit services for users across the broader Latin American region.

While managing a planned leadership transition for its global chief executive officer position, it successfully completed a $1 billion issuance of senior unsecured notes to institutional investors and expanded its marketplace delivery and pharmacy capabilities across Brazil.

Shopify: Experiencing Seasonal Spikes in Revenue Trends

Shopify (NASDAQ:SHOP) generates its revenue by providing an extensive digital commerce technology platform that equips independent global merchants with the necessary software tools to build digital storefronts, manage inventory, and fulfill their merchandise sales.

While navigating a California federal judge's recent refusal to dismiss a class action lawsuit regarding consumer data collection, it rolled out an extensive software update featuring new artificial intelligence integrations designed specifically for various merchant store checkouts.

Foolish Take

The first thing to check for when examining a company's revenue trend is seasonality: some times of the year have stronger buying patterns than others. There usually is some seasonality for every business.

We see this seasonality in both MercadoLibre and Shopify stocks, with the fourth calendar quarter of each year showing an uptick, followed by a drop-off into the first quarter. In these cases, comparing a quarter to the prior year's comparable quarter provides a better sense of the longer-term trend and helps adjust for seasonality.

But even with seasonality, we see two companies with strong sales trends looking right to left. The better results come from MercadoLibre, which shows its sales growth is so strong it almost totally offsets its seasonality. The company's push into financial services, moving beyond its traditional business of online retail business, is clearly paying dividends.

Interestingly, Shopify's revenue is growing faster quarter by quarter than the overall retail sector it serves. That implies it's grabbing market share.

The revenue trend is the most obvious metric for investors to examine when considering a stock. The chart shows two thriving businesses, though one is clearly accelerating faster in its sales generation.

Key Takeaways

Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office added 45% to its Sea stake in the third quarter, and the stock has fallen 26% since Sept. 30.

Big funds also bought Alibaba, Coupang and MercadoLibre in the quarter, and all but Coupang have fallen since.

Sea's revenue grew 43% last quarter, but its profit came in below expectations as it spent on AI and fought rivals for share.

At about 17x forward earnings, with analysts' average target 81% above the price, Sea looks like the best buy of the four.

Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office added 45% more shares of Sea (SE:NYSE) in the third quarter, according to its 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 16. Sea's stock is down 26% since then.

He had plenty of company. Big funds also bought Alibaba (BABA:NYSE), Coupang (CPNG:NYSE) and MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) in the quarter. Three of the four stocks are lower since then, and Sea, Alibaba and Coupang are each about half below their 52-week highs.

Druckenmiller wasn't the biggest buyer of Sea

Duquesne held 1.59 million Sea shares worth $155 million on Sept. 30. That made Sea its seventh-biggest position, at 3.7% of the $4.15 billion of US stocks its 13F holds.

Causeway Capital Management, a $62 billion firm, made a much bigger bet. It bought 9.19 million new shares worth $894 million, and Sea became 10.0% of its 13F stocks and its third-biggest holding. Dan Sundheim's D1 Capital added 118% to its stake, and Lone Pine Capital added 490%.

Not everyone bought. Chase Coleman's Tiger Global cut its stake 43%. Of the big funds that have filed for the quarter, nine bought Sea or added 20% or more, and four sold out or cut 20% or more. A 13F only shows what a fund held on Sept. 30, so the 26% drop is measured from the quarter-end price, and we don't know what any of these funds paid.

Sea beat on sales and missed on profit

Sea reported its third quarter on Nov. 10. Revenue rose 43% to $8.6 billion. Shopee, its e-commerce business, had its most profitable quarter ever, with adjusted EBITDA up 45% to $269 million.

But group adjusted EBITDA of $931 million fell short of the $990 million analysts expected, and Bloomberg put the miss down to higher AI spending and tougher e-commerce competition. Garena's bookings grew just 5.9%. Monee's revenue grew 64% while its adjusted EBITDA rose only 15.5%, as its loan book grew 60% to $12.6 billion. The board did add $1 billion to Sea's buyback.

Burry said that he expanded his Adobe holding at approximately $246.

Burry exited his Oracle puts and closed the last of his Caterpillar puts amid ongoing downward volatility in both stocks.

The investor is moving to donate a significant portion of his appreciated Alphabet shares, which he has owned since the COVID period.

'The Big Short' investor Michael Burry said on Monday that he closed some put positions while adding to long holdings including Adobe, MercadoLibre, QXO and Lululemon, and moved to donate a portion of long-held Alphabet shares.

Adobe Purchase And Outlook

Burry said that he expanded his Adobe holding at approximately $246, without clarifying the number of shares purchased. ADBE stock gained 1% on Monday to close at $246 after dropping nearly 30% year-to-date.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

"I continue to believe Adobe will successfully adapt, as will several other large software names, to the changing AI environment," Burry said. He noted that free substitutes for tools such as Adobe's Photoshop have existed for decades, yet Adobe has still grown revenue by 10% or more in each of the past four years.

In his view, Adobe's advantage lies in its standardized file formats, large installed base, enterprise contracts, and information security rather than superior AI models. Burry identifies the main risks as the cost of using external AI models and the pace of new subscription growth, but he argues the current valuation more than compensates for those concerns.

Puts Are Getting Expensive, Says Burry

Burry also exited his Oracle (ORCL) puts and closed the last of his Caterpillar (CAT) puts amid ongoing downward volatility in both stocks. He continues to hold a large put position in the VanEck Semiconductor ETF, along with puts on the Nasdaq 100, Nvidia, MetLife, and Palantir.

He noted that his overall short-put exposure "continues to grow in size, so trimming made sense." He is now looking at using outright short positions instead of or in addition to puts, because "puts, with the higher volatility of late, are getting expensive."

Burry's Additional Long Purchases

Beyond Adobe, Burry added to MercadoLibre (MELI) at about $1,480, elevating it to one of his largest positions alongside Australian retailer Temple & Webster. He also bought more QXO common stock near $12 and increased his Lululemon holding at roughly $106.

Lululemon's next earnings report is not expected until the second week of December, leaving the stock under pressure from a continued lack of new information, he said.

MELI stock closed 2% lower on Monday, while QXO and LULU dropped 5% and 0.18%, respectively.

Less Favorable View Of Prospects Spurs Donation For GOOG Holdings

Burry is moving to donate a significant portion of his appreciated Alphabet shares, which he has owned since the COVID period.

He characterized the donation as similar to a sale and said it reflects a less favorable view of Alphabet's prospects over the next five to six years.

How Did Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ADBE, GOOG, GOOGL, LULU and QXO stock was in 'bearish' territory at the time of writing, while sentiment around MELI was 'bullish.' Sentiment around CT stock was 'neutral' in the meantime.

title: Can MercadoLibre's GMV Growth Fuel Long-Term Earnings Gains?
detail:
Can MercadoLibre's GMV Growth Fuel Long-Term Earnings Gains?
Sumit Singh
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 8:07 AM MST 4 min read
MELI
AMZN
SE
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI continues to build momentum in Latin America's e-commerce market, supported by higher purchase frequency, expanding customer engagement and improving logistics efficiency. In third-quarter 2026, gross merchandise volume (GMV) reached $22.8 billion, increasing 38% year over year on a reported basis and 33% on an FX-neutral basis, while items sold rose 36% to 867 million. Unique active buyers increased approximately 22.3% to 93.9 million, highlighting sustained marketplace adoption and deeper customer engagement.

Brazil remains a major growth driver, with FX-neutral GMV advancing 36% and items sold rising 45%. The company's lower free-shipping threshold continues to encourage more frequent purchases, with items per buyer increasing 16% year over year. Management also reported stronger retention among customer cohorts acquired after the threshold reduction. However, smaller baskets and more free shipments have reduced shipping revenue per shipment. As a result, net shipping margin as a percentage of GMV has declined approximately 200 basis points since first-quarter 2025.

Meanwhile, Brazil's cost per shipment fell 5% year over year in local currency and 14% compared with first-quarter 2025, reflecting improving logistics efficiency. In September, free and slow shipments in the R$19-R$79 price range became variable contribution-positive for the first time. MercadoLibre is also expanding its logistics capabilities, having opened 13 Metro fulfillment centers over the past 12 months and more than doubled the number of sorters and robots across its network. Management expects higher shipment density, automation and better network utilization to drive further cost improvements.

Still, stronger GMV growth has yet to translate fully into operating profitability. Third-quarter operating income declined 6% year over year to $676 million, while the operating margin reached 6.3%, down 40 basis points sequentially. Net shipping costs created a 60-basis-point margin headwind, reflecting increased free shipping, higher energy expenses and additional fulfillment capacity. Increased affiliate marketing investments in Brazil also pressured margins. Nevertheless, net income rose 6% to $448 million, supported by a lower tax rate and reduced foreign-exchange losses.

Management expects improving logistics productivity and greater operating scale to gradually reduce shipping costs relative to business volumes. MercadoLibre's ability to sustain purchase frequency while lowering fulfillment costs remains central to translating marketplace growth into stronger long-term earnings.

How Has eBay's Growth Story Changed?

eBay (EBAY) stock trades at 25.6 times earnings, against 21.9 for the S&P 500. Shareholders paying that premium need to know what they are buying, yet management's priorities have changed. On its fiscal Q4 2024 call in February 2025, management emphasized a significant investment to overhaul consumer selling in the U.K., its second-largest market. On its latest call, management's U.K. remarks centered on consumer-selling growth, returns, and shipping initiatives. So what does management talk up now?

eBay Now Talks Up Depop Over Its U.K. Overhaul

On its fiscal Q3 2026 call on October 28, 2026, management said it is managing eBay and Depop as a portfolio. eBay recently acquired Depop, a secondhand fashion marketplace. Management called U.S. consumer fashion selling an underpenetrated market where it is building with two established brands, Depop and eBay.

Management said Depop's growth builds on eBay's consumer-selling momentum, the same business whose overhaul it made the case for in the U.K. in early 2025. On the fiscal Q4 2024 call, it said it had made a significant investment in its second-largest market through an overhaul of consumer selling in the U.K. On the fiscal Q2 2025 call in July 2025, management said growth in U.K. GMV, the value of goods sold, was comfortably above its level before that investment. eBay has since launched improvements to consumer selling in France and Italy, including free selling, but the U.K. overhaul no longer gets the airtime it once did.

Depop Is Growing Far Faster Than eBay Abroad

Depop's U.S. GMV more than doubled from a year earlier in fiscal Q3 2026, management said. Its active buyers over twelve months reached 11 million, up from 9 million. Depop is now part of eBay's totals: GMV grew nearly 16% to $23.2 billion before currency moves. Depop added nearly 3 points of that growth, and eBay grew 13% without it.

The U.K. sits inside eBay's international business, and that business grew far more slowly. International GMV grew nearly 4% in fiscal Q3 2026, against 22% for the U.S., both on an organic basis. Organic growth leaves out Depop.

Is Depop's Rise Good News For eBay Holders?

For the U.K., the change looks reassuring rather than worrying. Management said consumer-selling GMV grew more than 20% worldwide in fiscal Q3 2026, with healthy double-digit growth in the U.S., the U.K. and Australia. Even with less airtime, the business the overhaul set out to fix is still growing.

MercadoLibre has seen its share price fall sharply over the past year, and that slide has pushed investors to focus more squarely on what the current market value implies about its earnings power. Over the past 12 months, MercadoLibre's share price has declined 29%, which puts the spotlight on whether the earnings profile justifies the reset in market expectations.

Management is plowing significant cash into logistics, marketing, financial services and advertising partnerships, which can reshape both future earnings growth and the timing of when those profits show up in the income statement.

Is MercadoLibre Fairly Priced on Earnings?

The P/E ratio is a useful lens for MercadoLibre because earnings remain a key focus after the recent margin pressure. The stock currently trades on a P/E of 40.0x, which is roughly double the Multiline Retail industry average of 20.0x and also well above the peer group at 19.5x. That points to a valuation that leans heavily on what the market expects the business to earn over time rather than what it has already delivered.

MercadoLibre (MELI) stock fell approximately 20% from October 5 to November 10, closing at $1,490.24 after reaching a new 52-week low on November 5.

MercadoLibre's third-quarter revenue and financial income rose 45% to $10.75 billion, but operating margin declined to 6.3% as shipping, fulfillment, and marketing investments pressured profitability.

Sea Limited (SE) reported 41.3% revenue growth at Shopee in the third quarter, while Nu Holdings (NU) provides another perspective on Brazilian consumer credit conditions.

MercadoLibre appears potentially undervalued following the selloff, although stronger margins and continued market share gains will be important to a sustained recovery.

What Happened?

MercadoLibre (MELI) stock declined approximately 20% from its October 5 closing price of $1,860.61 to $1,490.24 on November 10, after hitting a new 52-week low on November 5.

The decline reflects two concerns: political uncertainty in Brazil and weaker-than-expected profitability despite strong revenue growth.

Brazil's October 25 presidential runoff delivered another term for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who defeated Flávio Bolsonaro after trailing him in the first round.

MercadoLibre shares fell approximately 8% on October 26 as investors reassessed Brazil's economic outlook, currency risks, and consumer spending conditions.

Brazil generated approximately $15.2 billion of MercadoLibre's $28.9 billion in 2025 revenue, making it the company's largest market.

However, the company's third-quarter earnings report created a more immediate concern.

According to MercadoLibre's third-quarter financial results, revenue and financial income increased 45% year over year to $10.75 billion, but reported earnings of $8.83 per share fell short of the $9.27 consensus estimate cited in the initial research brief.

Operating margin declined to 6.3% from approximately 9.8% a year earlier, reflecting higher shipping expenses, expanded fulfillment capacity, and increased marketing spending in Brazil.

In its third-quarter shareholder letter, management described the pressure on shipping margins as "the price of the habit we set out to build."

The strategy is producing results. Items sold in Brazil increased more than 40% year over year for the fifth consecutive quarter, while MercadoLibre gained market share across its three largest markets.

Its lower free-shipping threshold also encouraged smaller purchases, initially putting pressure on shipping economics.

By September, Brazilian orders valued between R$19 and R$79 that qualified for free or slower delivery became variable contribution-positive for the first time, suggesting higher order volumes are beginning to improve shipping economics.

Key Takeaways

MercadoLibre stock fell 10% in the week to Nov. 10 after third-quarter EPS came in at $8.83, short of the $9.27 analysts expected, even as revenue rose 45%.

Management chose the squeeze, spending on free shipping and warehouses while Sea Limited's Shopee keeps gaining in Brazil.

Brazil's cost per shipment is falling, and credit held steady, a bar for Nu Holdings ahead of its expected Nov. 12 report.

Analysts still expect an earnings rebound, and the stock trades far below its usual forward multiple.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) stock fell 10% from Nov. 3 to Nov. 10, with most of the damage in a 12% drop on Nov. 5, the day after its report. Revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion, but EPS of $8.83 missed the $9.27 expected.

That spending comes as Shopee, owned by Sea Limited (SE:NYSE), pushes harder in Brazil, which Sea said on Nov. 10 was again its fastest-growing market. And MercadoLibre's credit sets a bar for Nu Holdings (NU:NYSE), which is expected to report on Nov. 12.

The miss was a choice

Operating income fell 6.6% to $676 million, a 6.3% margin against 9.8% a year earlier. The company paid for more free shipping, added fulfillment space ahead of the holidays and stepped up affiliate marketing in Brazil. CEO Ariel Szarfsztejn told analysts the company is spending because the opportunity in front of it is large. "We have accepted a lower margin to do that," he said.

But the shipping bill is starting to shrink: Brazil's cost per shipment fell 5% from a year earlier in local currency. And in September, orders between R19andR79, which now ship free, paid their own variable costs for the first time.

Shopee is pushing just as hard. It launched four-hour delivery in greater São Paulo in August with more than 4,000 partner stores, and Sea said on Nov. 10 that the service now runs from more than 7,000. MercadoLibre began testing one-hour delivery in parts of the city in September. Sea also said Shopee again grew faster than Brazil's broader market in the third quarter.

Analysts still see a rebound

Analysts still expect a sharp rebound:

MercadoLibre (MELI): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2029 (TIKR)

But the 2027 figure is down more than a third from where it stood in September 2025, so the rebound has been pushed out before.

Credit held up, with loans 15 to 90 days late at 7.0% of a portfolio that grew 62% in a year to about $18 billion. Nu's ratio was 4.8% in the second quarter, and its next results will show whether its Brazil book is holding up as well.

The stock is cheap against its own history:

MercadoLibre (MELI): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

It traded at 34x on Nov. 9, far below its five-year average of 62x and not far above its five-year low of about 30x.

If the margin recovers as the network fills, today's multiple could reward investors who wait out the squeeze. The holiday quarter is the first test: CFO Martin de los Santos expects part of the capacity cost to reverse in the fourth quarter as volumes rise, though higher energy costs may linger.
